planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring before shoots emerge, or in fall, into moist, humus-rich woodland soil in partial to full shade; mulch with leaf litter to mimic its native forest-floor conditions.

directions: A whorled-leaf Solomon's seal from a colder, more northerly native range spanning Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning, Inner Mongolia, Korea, and the Russian Far East, this species gives cold-climate gardeners a hardier whorled-leaf option with narrower, more numerous leaves than its already-cultivated relatives. Its colder native provenance sets it apart texturally and makes it a useful companion for extending whorled-leaf interest through a shade border. Like its whorled relatives, it spreads slowly by thick rhizome into a long-lived colony rather than running aggressively, and keeping soil from drying out is especially important while the clump is establishing.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online
